reason: The GitHub Copilot integration hooks and scripts fail multiple portability, dependency, and safety checks. They are not suitable for adoption as Aether-first-party artifacts. Consumer-specific hook wiring belongs to Empathy, not Aether.
safety_concerns: session-start.sh requires Taskfile.yml to be present in the repository root; this file is absent from the current snapshot. The hook fails with an unintelligible error rather than a safe diagnostic.
session-start.sh uses GNU 'date --date' syntax, which is not portable to macOS BSD 'date'. Declared macOS compatibility is therefore false.
Shell scripts in the snapshot are not executable (missing +x bit); they cannot run as written.
pre-tool-use.sh validates tool names but lacks JSON payload fixtures to test valid, invalid, malicious, missing-tool, and privacy cases.
error-occurred.sh logs error messages that may contain private content from agent responses.
The hooks.json wires all three events (sessionStart, preToolUse, errorOccurred) without documenting which events are opt-in and which are always-on.
No PowerShell parity is verified between .sh and .ps1 variants; behavioral divergence is undocumented.
adoption_blocked_by: Non-portable GNU date syntax breaks macOS.
Consumer-specific wiring belongs to Empathy, not Aether.
Error logging may capture private agent response content.
